solver.method: depth-averaged shallow water, Rusanov flux with hydrostatic reconstruction, Bingham bed stress
solver.label: synthetic breach scenario of a hypothetical facility on real terrain, not validated against real data

scenarios.label: Reference: 100,000 m3, 100 Pa
scenarios.source: volume, yield stress, viscosity and density: inside the training envelope of the C2 surrogate (specs/011-surrogates contract example surrogate-io.valid-fno.json, training_envelope: volume 1e4 to 2e5 m3, yield stress 10 to 200 Pa, plastic viscosity 0.05 to 1 Pa s, density 1600 to 2000 kg/m3), values taken mid-range; peak discharge = volume x 422 / 3.8e6 per second, the ratio of the Mirai reconstruction (3.8 Mm3 released, 422 m3/s peak: Silva and Eleuterio 2023, NHESS 23:3095, quoted in docs/cases/c2-tailings-breach.md; the paper itself was not read: UNVERIFIED), base time T = 2 V / Q_p (FR-005-31)

scenarios.label: Fluid: 100,000 m3, 10 Pa
scenarios.source: yield stress and plastic viscosity at the lower bound of the training envelope (10 Pa, 0.05 Pa s); volume, density and hydrograph as the reference scenario

scenarios.label: Large: 200,000 m3, 100 Pa
scenarios.source: volume at the upper bound of the training envelope (2e5 m3); peak discharge = volume x 422 / 3.8e6 per second as the reference scenario; rheology and density as the reference scenario

limits.educational, not regulatory: a depth-averaged 2-D flow with a single-phase Bingham rheology, no erosion, entrainment or breach mechanics

limits: the facility, its volume and its breach are hypothetical scenario inputs; there is no real flood record for this terrain, so the fields are calibrated synthetic and not validated against real data

the bed force of the first-order hydrostatic reconstruction on a slope is smaller than the exact one by the factor S dx / (2 h) (slope S, cell dx, depth h); on steep cells with shallow flow the front runs slower than the exact equations would give
the Ritter front at the specified 1e-3 h_l threshold lags the analytical front by 14 to 21 percent (FR-005-24 asks 5 percent); at 0.1 h_l it is within 3 percent
the pit walls are steeper than the long-wave assumption of the shallow-water equations allows, so the flow on them is indicative
